diagnostic_evidence.quote: The set $\{ \bs{s}_{j,j} \mm \tU_{:,j} \}_{j=1}^r$ is a minimal generating set for $\operatorname{Image}(T_{\tX})$ when considered as $\FFF_n$-module.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof only shows that for each j some generator W_k has nonzero inner product with s_{j,j}*U_{:,j}; nothing prevents the same k from serving every j, so the inference r' >= r is a non sequitur. The statement itself is true (the minimal number of generators of the image equals max_j lambda_j, which equals the number of nonzero singular tubes), but this requires a different argument, e.g. projecting onto a block e_j with maximal tubal-length and using linear independence over the field F^{(j)}.

failure_location.quote: Showing that for all $j \in [r]$ there exists $k \in [r']$ such that $\bs{s}_{j,j} \mm \vec{\matW}_k^\CT \mm  \tU_{:,j} \neq \bs{0}$, hence $r' \geq r$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the last step by: pick j* with lambda_{j*} = r; applying e_{j*} to any generating set of size r' gives a spanning set of the r-dimensional F^{(j*)}-vector space V_{j*}, hence r' >= r.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma lem:tensor.hom.range.gen is unproved as written; it is only used as motivation for Definition def:t-rank, so no downstream result is invalidated.
issues.title: Minimality of the generating set is not established by the given argument
issues.why_classification: The claim is correct and the missing argument is a short, local, routine replacement; nothing else depends on it.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Since $\bs{p}_j \mm \tU_{:,j} \neq \bs{0}$, the set $\{ k_h \}_{h=1}^{r'} \subseteq [r]$ such that $\bs{p}_j \mm \bs{z}_{j,k_h} \neq \bs{0}$ for all $h = 1, \ldots, r'$ is nonempty.

issues.failure_explanation: The argument only knows p_j * z_{j,k_h} != 0, but the displayed relation has coefficients t_j * z_{j,k_h} with t_j = e - p_j; these can all vanish (e.g. z_{j,k} in <p_j>), in which case the combination is trivial and nothing is shown. The conclusion (the image is not free when some p_j != e) is true, but for a different reason: the image is a direct sum of vector spaces V_j of unequal dimensions, whereas a free module of rank r has all block dimensions equal to r.

failure_location.quote: which is a nontrivial linear combination of elements of $B$ that equals zero, therefore no generating set of $\operatorname{Image}(T_{\tX})$ can be a basis

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the argument: if B were a basis of size r then applying e_j shows dim V_j = r for every j, contradicting the fact that p_j != e forces some block dimension to be smaller than another.
issues.overall_effect: The motivating example for abandoning module rank in favour of module length is unsupported as written; no labelled result depends on it.
issues.title: Non-freeness example asserts a 'nontrivial' relation without showing its coefficients are nonzero
issues.why_classification: The claim is true and the corrected argument is short and local; the example is purely motivational.

issues.failure_explanation: From eq. nec.intra.Frob.norm.tA.tB.gamma and the displayed mixed-term expansion, the correct formula is ||A-B||^2 = S||D||^2 + 2Re(g)(||Re D||^2-||Im D||^2) - 4Im(g)<Re D,Im D>, but eq. nec.intra.Frob.norm.tA.tB.final flips both signs. With the correct signs, ||A-A^{(1)}||^2 = |alpha_2|^2(S-2Re g) and ||A-A^{(2)}||^2 = alpha_1^2(S+2Re g) (directly: ||c_s ± c_{s'}||^2 = S ± 2Re g), so with the paper's choice |alpha_2|^2 = alpha_1^2 (S-2Re g)/(S+Re g) the truncation A_{Λ} is in fact the better approximation in both sign cases (the difference of errors is alpha_1^2 x(2x-7S)/(S+x) with x=Re g, |x|<=S/2), and the claimed violation does not occur. The same sign flip makes the second example (for Im g) fail in both cases (difference y(7S+2y)). Moreover the tensor A^{(2)} in the second example is not real, since its slice s' is -alpha E_2 rather than the conjugate alpha E_2 of slice s. The lemma's conclusion is nevertheless true: with correct signs one can choose |alpha_2|/|alpha_1| strictly between 1 and sqrt((S+2x)/(S-2x)) (or its reciprocal) to obtain a genuine violation, and analogously for Im g.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the signs in eq. nec.intra.Frob.norm.tA.tB.final, fix A^{(2)} to be real, and re-select the scalar ratios (|alpha_2|/|alpha_1| and a) so that the truncated component has slightly larger singular value but strictly larger weighted error, using ||A-A^{(1)}||^2=|alpha_2|^2(S-2Re g), ||A-A^{(2)}||^2=alpha_1^2(S+2Re g) and the analogous Im g formulas.
issues.overall_effect: As written, the necessity direction of the main theorem (rows within an idempotent block must be orthogonal, hence equal norm) rests on a proof whose counterexamples do not violate optimality; the theorem's 'only if' part is unsupported until the construction is redone.
issues.title: Sign error in the Frobenius-norm expansion invalidates both counterexamples in the intra-idempotent necessity proof
issues.why_classification: The lemma and main theorem survive, but the entire necessity construction must be recomputed and its parameters re-chosen; this is a contained but non-mechanical repair of a proof supporting the paper's central 'only if' claim.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The following result shows normalization of the transform's rows always improves compression performance in this sense.

issues.failure_explanation: In Algorithm alg:tSVDMII the energy ratio beta under M_1 = DQ is computed from the scaled singular values (mu_k^2 s_{jjk}^2)/||S~||^2, whereas ||X - X_{r^{(1)}}||_F^2/||X||_F^2 is the unscaled quantity (M_0 is unitary and X_{r^{(1)}} is the same truncation under M_0). The proof's equality 1-beta_{r_gamma(M_1)} = ||X-X_{r^{(1)}}||^2/||X||^2 is therefore false for non-identity D. The theorem fails outright: take n=2, M_0=I, M_1=diag(10,1), X the tube (1,1), gamma=0.9. Under M_0, nu=(1,1), omega=(0.5,1), r_gamma(M_0)=2; under M_1, nu=(100,1), omega=(100/101,1), r_gamma(M_1)=1 < 2. (The step equating the number of discarded values with n·min(m,p)-r_gamma also ignores ties in line rhoi.def, but the counterexample is independent of ties.)

failure_location.quote: Then for all $\tX \in \RR^{m \xx p \xx n}$ and $\gamma \in (0,1)$, we have $r_{\gamma} (\matM_0) \leq r_{\gamma} (\matM_1)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must withdraw the inequality r_gamma(M_0) <= r_gamma(M_1) for the algorithm as written and replace it with a materially different statement, e.g. one in which the energy retention criterion is measured in the true Frobenius norm (then selection by unscaled singular values is optimal by rearrangement), which changes the algorithm/criterion being compared.
issues.overall_effect: The 'no-go result' that row normalization never worsens the tSVDMII compression rank is false, so the surrounding claims ('the effect of non-uniform scaling of the transform's rows on the compression rates is necessarily detrimental', 'always improves compression performance in this sense', and the Conclusions' statement that scaled transforms are not beneficial for compression) are unsupported. Lemma lem:normalized.mrtrunk.eq and Theorem thm:fixed.rank.DW.vs.W remain valid.
issues.title: Theorem thm:gamma.DW.vs.W is false: scaled-domain energy ratios are conflated with true relative error
issues.why_classification: The stated theorem admits an explicit counterexample and no comparable version of the claim about Algorithm alg:tSVDMII survives; any fix changes the quantity being compared.
